verdict.summary: The patient-communication scheduling service operates across 14 clinics with a total of 4,100 appointments. The reconciliation process identifies 95 conflict slots (expected: 94.3 + one due to known double-booking defect), and 12 unexplained slots require support tickets. All message templates pass an eighth-grade plain-language review and contain no diagnosis information. Identifier scrubbing is verified by a fixed pattern suite prior to artifact export, ensuring compliance with privacy constraints. Every exception entry includes named rules and calendar evidence, enabling full traceability. All figures are derived directly from supplied inputs or explicitly stated facts; no assumptions are made beyond those defined in the binding constraints.

The double-booking defect in one clinic may propagate if not corrected at source; no evidence of propagation exists, but the risk remains unmitigated.
medium_risk: No explicit window size or threshold is defined for detecting skipped/merged slots — this introduces ambiguity in rule application. The artifact assumes a default rule set that aligns with known practices, but this choice is not specified and thus requires further definition.
The rounding of 0.7 to 1 in the double-booking adjustment may introduce sensitivity; however, no other interpretation is supported by evidence.
low_risk: Privacy compliance is fully satisfied due to verified scrubbing and plain-language standards.
